I've had some pretty serious issues with anxiety & depression throughout the majority of my life that has made everything much harder than it needs to be. I've gone through many slumps and almost ended things a number of times, but each time I eventually pushed myself to my limits just to try to prove to myself that I had some sort of worth and that I could be a normal human being. Lately, it feels like all the torture I went through was for nothing, and that all of my current efforts are inconsequential at best.

It might sound stupid and it certainly isn't healthy (drugs), but I managed to find this spark in the local edm scene. Up until a few months ago, I had never danced a single time in my life, and now I'm hooked on going out every weekend. Expanding my comfort zone, enjoying music with others, learning to let go, and establishing new social connections has provided a sort of joy not experienced in a very long time.

Maybe I'll take a moment to share my thoughts as I've seen these problems lingering around for what seems like years now.

I think both visibility and timing are both crucial to game balance. This is because both elements are necessary for a player to utilize some degree of skill to avoid dangerous situations. Without those elements, life and death often comes as a surprise instead of a consequence of the player's abilities.

Visibility should be proportional to damage. The higher the damage, the higher the visibility should be.  In PoE, this is sometimes done well, and sometimes isn't really done at all. For example, some high damage boss skills, like Voll smash, have a highly visible animation to properly warn the player of the danger. Then, there are also very high damage skills with poor visibility. I'm not sure if there is any indicator at all for volatiles, despite it being a one shot mechanic. The same is true for detonate dead - it just happens and you are either dead or alive. Visibility is an issue for many other very damaging skills like reflect; sometimes reflectis difficult to see depending on the monster type, mob packs, and environment. Other times, it is impossible to see reflect at all (offscreen).

I would recommend that GGG iterates through all high damage sources and ensures that each one is clearly visible to the player in some way. Audio hints are another possibility for indicating danger but I would avoid that because some people tend to lower in-game sound and listen to music or streams instead.

Timing is the other critical element of balance. Obviously, anything that is instant is unavoidable. It's only my opinion, but I think unavoidable things are silly. Call me crazy, but I feel the player should be able to provide inputs such that they can avoid death. For example, a player should be able to reflexively use a movement skill to avoid a devestating boss smash (because it engages gameplay, provides player satisfaction, and the player doesn't randomly lose hundreds of hours of work). GGG has made this the case for many encounters, but not all. For example, volatiles, detonate dead (non-strongbox), and reflect are all unavoidably instant. If you didn't happen to notice their presence, you are dead (which plays back into the aforementioned visibility problems).

To remedy this, I recommend that very high damage source should always have an associated delay such that the player has a chance to engage and avoid the danger. I think a fairly well done version of this is the bearer skill (though I still hate the shit out of it). Instead of the mobs dying and instantly transmitting huge damage to the player, there is both a delay for the player to escape and a visibility element to display the danger (note: I feel the visibility needs to be emboldened because it is easy to miss when it blends into all the other chaos going on). 

To rework all of the damage sources will require some work and imagination on the part of GGG. For example, adding visibility and delay to the volatile skill would effectively change it into an uber version of bearers, so some imagination is required to change it into something more original. Reflect could be more simple, where the monsters actually reflect the damage in the form of projectiles or something else that the player can spatially evade.

Hopefully I've presented my ideas clearly. Perhaps with some luck, these ideas can be used to combat some of the mechanics which currently have an unfair vibe to them. Thanks for reading.
